h: Blessing and Protection Within the Heart

p: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (רמח סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳), יְבָרֶכְךָ הַשֵּׁם וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ,
— The holy Zohar on this portion (248a, end) teaches: “May Hashem bless you and guard you.”
יְבָרֶכְךָ הַשֵּׁם מִדְּכוּרָא, וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ מִנּוּקְבָא,
— “May Hashem bless you” is from the masculine aspect; “and guard you” is from the feminine aspect.
יְבָרֶכְךָ הַשֵּׁם מִזָּכוֹר, וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ מִשָּׁמוֹר.
— “May Hashem bless you” comes from “remember”; “and guard you” comes from “keep.”
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ צב סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳), זָכוֹר לִדְכוּרָא וְשָׁמוֹר לְנוּקְבָא,
— This accords with the teaching (Zohar III, 92b, end): “remember” belongs to the masculine and “keep” to the feminine.
וְהוּא מִדַּת יוֹם וּמִדַּת לַיְלָה כַּיָּדוּעַ.
— These are the attributes of day and night, as is known.
וְזֶהוּ וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ, הַשְּׁמִירָה מִכָּל רַע,
— This is “and guard you”: protection from every evil.
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת הַיִּרְאָה לִהְיוֹת סוּר מֵרָע,
— This comes through the aspect of fear, enabling one to turn from evil,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁכִינָה, דְּאִיהִי יִרְאָה וְכוּלֵי.
— through the holiness of the Divine Presence, which is fear, and so forth.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רל א) עַל פָּסוּק הַמַּלְאָךְ הַגּוֹאֵל אוֹתִי, דָּא שְׁכִינְתָּא וְכוּלֵי,
— As the holy Zohar says (230a) on “the angel who redeems me”: this is the Divine Presence, and so forth.
וְהוּא הַגּוֹאֵל מִכָּל רַע כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ מִשְׁכַּן הַשְּׁכִינָה בַּלֵּב,
— It is what redeems from every evil when the Divine Presence dwells in the heart,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם.
— meaning that one possesses fear of Heaven.
שֶׁמִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם דָּרְשׁוּ (יוֹמָא עב:) וְלֶב אָיִן,
— Concerning one who lacks fear of Heaven, they expound (Yoma 72b), “and he has no heart.”
דְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא דְּשַׁרְיָא בֵּיהּ יִרְאָה, וְאָז הוּא נִגְאָל מִכָּל רַע.
— For an Israelite heart is one in which fear dwells; then he is redeemed from every evil.
וְזֶה מִדַּת לַיְלָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וֶאֱמוּנָתְךָ בַּלֵּילוֹת,
— This is the attribute of night, as it says, “And Your faithfulness in the nights,”
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ רל א), אִיהִי אֱמוּנָה.
— following the teaching of Raya Mehemna (Zohar III, 230a): she is faith.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 248a; Zohar, Vayechi 77:800: “He opened and said: “May Hashem bless you from Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem.” “May Hashem bless you from Zion”—from there blessings emerge to water the garden. He comprises all blessings and gives them to her; afterward, “may you see the good of Jerusalem.” This shows that all blessings come from male and female. Likewise, “May Hashem bless you and guard you”: “May Hashem bless you”—from the male; “and guard you”—from the female. “May Hashem bless you”—from “Remember”; “and guard you”—from “Keep.” It is all one matter, because from both of them blessings issue to the worlds. Therefore: “Each man according to his blessing, he blessed them.””

If “Keep” belongs to the female, why is it written, “You shall keep My commandments”?”

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 230a; Zohar, Vayechi 42:425: “He opened and said: “The angel who redeems me from all evil.” This verse must be examined. Why does it say “who redeems,” rather than “who redeemed”? Because he is constantly present with people and never departs from a righteous person. Come and see: “The angel who redeems me”—this is the Shechinah, which goes with a person continually and does not depart when he keeps the Torah’s commandments. Therefore a person must take care not to go alone on the road. What does “alone” mean? He must take care to keep the Torah’s commandments, so that the Shechinah will not depart from him and leave him to travel alone, without her companionship.”

p: יְבָרֶכְךָ, הַיְינוּ הַהַשְׁפָּעָה בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה לְלֵב חָכָם לִימִינוֹ.
— “May He bless you” signifies the influx of Torah teachings into the wise heart on its right.
וּבָזֶה כְּתִיב יְבָרֶכְךָ הַשֵּׁם בְּשֵׁם הֲוָיָה, וְהוּא מִדַּת יוֹם,
— Concerning this it says “May Hashem bless you,” using the Name Havayah, and it corresponds to the attribute of day,
כְּמָה דְאַתְּ אָמַר וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם, וּכְתִיב וְתוֹרָה אוֹר.
— as it says, “God called the light day”; and it is written, “Torah is light.”
וְהוּא שֵׁם הֲוָיָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ (בְּרָכוֹת כא.) לְבִרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה לְפָנֶיהָ,
— This is the Name Havayah, as expounded (Berakhot 21a) regarding the blessing before Torah study,
מִדִּכְתִיב כִּי שֵׁם הַשֵּׁם אֶקְרָא הָבוּ גוֹדֶל וְגוֹמֵר.
— from “For I shall proclaim the name of Hashem; ascribe greatness,” and so forth.
וְאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ, וְכֹלָּא חַד מִלָּה, בְּגִין דְּמִתְּרַוַּויְיהוּ נָפְקִין בִּרְכָאן לְעָלְמִין.
— The holy Zohar says: all is one matter, for blessings issue from both of them to the worlds.

h: Making a Dwelling in Both Chambers

p: וּבְשַׁבָּת כְּתִיב וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי, וְלֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ אֵיזֶה בְרָכָה.
— Concerning Shabbat it says, “God blessed the seventh day,” without specifying which blessing.
וּבְוַדַּאי קָאֵי עַל הַבְּרָכָה הַמְּפוֹרֶשֶׁת בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר, וְהוּא בִּרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים.
— It certainly refers to the blessing specified elsewhere: the priestly blessing.
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר (תִּקּוּן מח), מַאי לְדֹרֹתָם,
— This is as Tikkunei Zohar, tikkun 48, teaches: what does “throughout their generations” signify?
זַכָּאָה מַאן דְּעָבֵיד לוֹן דִּירָה בְּשַׁבָּת בִּתְרֵי בָּתֵּי לִבָּא וְכוּלֵי.
— Fortunate is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the heart’s two chambers, and so forth.
וְהוּא לְהוֹרִיק הָרַע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ,
— This means emptying evil from the foolish heart on its left,
וּלְהַכְנִיס הַקְּדוּשָּׁה וְהַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּלֵב חָכָם לִימִינוֹ.
— and bringing holiness and words of Torah into the wise heart on its right.
וְשׁוֹכֵן שְׁכִינְתָּא עִלָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה בִּשְׁנֵי חַלְלֵי הַלֵּב, וְזֶהוּ יְבָרֶכְךָ וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ כָּאָמוּר.
— The upper and lower Divine Presence dwell in the two cavities of the heart: this is “May He bless you and guard you,” as explained.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Nasso 10:1: “It appears that the Ramban explains the priestly blessing as being like the blessing of Shabbat. That is why on ‘May He bless you and guard you’ he brought ‘remember’ and ‘keep,’ and on ‘and be gracious to you’ he brought their Midrash on the Shabbat day. For it is written, ‘God blessed the seventh day,’ without specifying with what He blessed it, and presumably it is with the priestly blessing that is spelled out in the Torah. There is proof for his words from what the holy Zohar says (Ra’aya Meheimna, Pinchas 245a) about the secret of the twelve loaves, which correspond to the three Names Havayah in the verses ‘May He bless,’ ‘May He shine,’ ‘May He lift.’ And at every Shabbat meal twelve loaves are set out like the showbread; that is, the blessing of Shabbat is one with the priestly blessing.”

p: וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (לְעֵיל רלג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳) אִיתָא,
— The holy Zohar teaches above (233b, end):
כָּל בִּרְכָאן עִלָּאִין כֻּלְּהוּ אִתְמַסְּרוּ לְהַאי דַּרְגָּא וְכוּלֵי.
— All supernal blessings have been entrusted to this level, and so forth.
וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לָהּ נְהוֹרָא מִגַּרְמָהּ,
— Although she has no light of her own,
כָּל בִּרְכָאן וְכָל חֵידוּ וְכָל טִיבוּ כֻּלְּהוּ קָיְימִין בַּהּ וּמִינַהּ נָפְקֵי.
— all blessings, all joy, and all goodness abide within her and flow forth from her.
וְעַל דָּא אִתְקְרִיאַת כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה,
— Therefore she is called the cup of blessing,
כְּמָה דִכְתִיב בִּרְכַּת הַשֵּׁם הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר, וְעַל דָּא כְּתִיב וּמָלֵא בִּרְכַּת הַשֵּׁם וְגוֹמֵר.
— as it is written, “The blessing of Hashem brings wealth,” and thus it says, “Full of the blessing of Hashem,” and so forth.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּוַדַּאי כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת הֵם מֵעַתִּיקָא וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ,
— Certainly all blessings derive from Atika, as we explained.
וּמִדַּת מַלְכוּת הִיא בְּחִינַת הַסִּיהֲרָא דְּלֵית לָהּ מִגַּרְמָהּ כְּלוּם,
— The attribute of Malkhut corresponds to the moon, possessing nothing of its own.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת עַל יְדֵי מִדָּה זוֹ.
— Nevertheless, all blessings pass through this attribute.
וְכֵן כָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג׳ קמה סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳, קמו א), יְבָרְכוּכָה, יְבָרְכוּ כֹּה,
— So it is written in the holy Zohar (III, 145b, end; 146a): yevarkhukhah—“they shall bless Koh.”
דְּמִדַּת מַלְכוּת אִקְרֵי כֹּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם.
— For Malkhut is called Koh, as taught there.
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם רי ב),
— The holy Zohar teaches (ibid., 210b):
הֲרֵי כֹּה דְּזַמִּינָא לְבָרְכָא לוֹן, כֹּה תְּמַלֵּל בְּרָכָה דִּבְנַי וְכוּלֵי.
— Here is Koh, ready to bless them; Koh shall utter the blessing of My children, and so forth.
וְהַיְינוּ דְּמִדַּת שַׁבָּת כָּלִיל כָּל בִּרְכָאן וּמִינֵּיהּ מִתְבָּרְכָאן,
— The attribute of Shabbat thus includes all blessings, and from it they are blessed.
וְהַהַמְשָׁכָה עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהוּא הַנָּהָר דְּנָגִיד וְנָפִיק לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן, שְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה.
— The influx comes through Joseph, the river that flows forth to water the garden, the lower Divine Presence.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב שֶׁבֵּירַךְ יַעֲקֹב לְיוֹסֵף, דְּכָל בִּרְכָא אִתְמַסְּרוּ בִּידֵיהּ לְבָרְכָא,
— This is why Jacob blessed Joseph: all blessings were entrusted to his hand, to bestow blessing,
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר לְמַעְלָה מַאֲמָר ז).
— as explained above in discourse 7.
וְחָשַׁב כָּל בִּרְכָאן, דְּהוּא מְקוֹר הַבְּרָכָה,
— It enumerated all blessings, for he is the source of blessing.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Ramban, Bereishis 2:3: “‘And He blessed and sanctified’: He blessed it with the manna and sanctified it with the manna, and the verse is written with reference to the future; these are the words of Rashi from Bereishis Rabbah. In the name of the Gaon Rav Saadiah they said that the blessing and sanctification refer to those who keep it, that they will be blessed and sanctified. If you understand these words of mine, you will know what they said in Bereishis Rabbah, ‘because it has no partner,’ and what they further said, ‘the Congregation of Israel shall be your partner,’ and you will grasp that on Shabbat there is truly an additional soul.”

h: Shabbat Gives Light and Torah Wealth

p: וְכֵן יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת כְּלָלָא דְּכָל בִּרְכָאן וְכָל חֵידוּ וְכָל טִיבוּ.
— Likewise Shabbat encompasses all blessings, all joy, and all goodness.
טִיבוּ מוֹרֶה עַל בְּחִינַת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב,
— “Goodness” signifies the aspect of “the light, that it was good.”
וּכְתִיב אוֹר זָרוּעַ לַצַּדִּיק, וּכְתִיב אוֹר צַדִּיקִים יִשְׂמָח.
— It is written, “Light is sown for the righteous,” and “The light of the righteous rejoices.”
שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ עַל יְדֵי הָאוֹר שֶׁהוּא לַצַּדִּיקִים זוֹכִין לְייַשֵּׁר הַלֵּב מִכֹּל וָכֹל וְזוֹכִין לְשִׂמְחָה.
— Thereafter, through the light granted to the righteous, one merits to straighten the heart completely and attain joy.
וְזֶהוּ וְכָל חֵידוּ וְכָל טִיבוּ, יְשָׁרִים לְשִׂמְחָה וְצַדִּיקִים לָאוֹרָה,
— This is “all joy and all goodness”: the upright are destined for joy, and the righteous for light,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סוֹף פֶּרֶק א׳ דְּתַעֲנִית).
— as taught at the end of the first chapter of Taanit.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁמִּתְיַישֵּׁר הַלֵּב מִכֹּל וָכֹל, שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר כָּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִלִּבּוֹ,
— This is when the heart becomes completely upright and the entire evil inclination is uprooted from it,
שֶׁהוּא כְּשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְשַׁבָּת עִלָּאָה, וְאִתְפַּנֵּי מִתַּמָּן יֵצֶר הָרָע (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תִּיקּוּן מח).
— when one attains the higher Shabbat, from which the evil inclination is removed (as taught in tikkun 48).
וּכְתִיב בִּרְכַּת הַשֵּׁם הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר, וְהַיְינוּ עֲשִׁירוּת בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה,
— It is written, “The blessing of Hashem brings wealth”: wealth in Torah teachings,
וּכְעֵין מַה שֶּׁנִּדְרַשׁ (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא תִּשָּׂא ג), וְהַשָּׂבָע לֶעָשִׁיר,
— resembling the exposition (Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tissa 3) of “the rich man’s abundance”:
בַּעֲשִׁירֵי תוֹרָה אֲנִי מְדַבֵּר וְלֹא בַּעֲשִׁירֵי מָמוֹן.
— I speak of those wealthy in Torah, rather than those wealthy in money.
וְכֵן בַּגְּמָרָא (תְּמוּרָה טז.) נִדְרַשׁ עָשִׁיר וָרָשׁ נִפְגָּשׁוּ, מִי שֶׁעָשָׂה חָכָם לָזֶה וְכוּלֵי.
— Likewise the Gemara (Temurah 16a) expounds “The rich and poor meet”: He who made this one wise, and so forth.
וְכֵן (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה יא) אִיתָא בִּרְכַּת הַשֵּׁם הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר, זוֹ הַשַּׁבָּת,
— Likewise Bereishit Rabbah, beginning of chapter 11, teaches: “The blessing of Hashem brings wealth”—this is Shabbat,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי.
— as it says, “God blessed the seventh day.”
וְאָז הָיָה אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן יָחִיד בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם, וּמַה שַּׁיָּיךְ לוֹ בִּרְכַּת הָעוֹשֶׁר?
— At that time Adam was alone in the entire world, so what relevance did a blessing of wealth have to him?
רַק הַמְכוּוָּן עַל בְּרָכָה בַּעֲשִׁירוּת דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא בְּשַׁבָּת,
— Rather, it means the blessing of wealth in Torah that is found on Shabbat.
דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בְּשַׁבָּת נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב.
— All agree that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat, meaning the Written Torah.
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א׳ מז ב), בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה דְּאִיהוּ יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי.
— The holy Zohar (I, 47b) teaches: “On the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day.
וְהַיְינוּ מַלְכוּת, פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
— This is Malkhut, the mouth, the Oral Torah.
וְהַמְשָׁכַת הַבְּרָכָה עַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף,
— The drawing down of blessing is through Joseph,
שֶׁנֶּחְשָׁב בְּזֹהַר חָדָשׁ (תּוֹלְדוֹת) מוּסַף שַׁבָּת, שֶׁהוּא רִיבּוּי הַבְּרָכָה דְּשַׁבָּת, כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף וְכָאָמוּר.
— for Zohar Chadash, Toldot, associates Shabbat Musaf, the increase of Shabbat’s blessing, with Joseph’s aspect, as explained.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vaera 4:6: “Regarding Shabbat it says, ‘and He adds no sorrow with it,’ for on the Shabbat day Hashem, blessed be He, enlightens one’s eyes in words of Torah, so that they become absorbed forever and gladden his heart, as it says, ‘The precepts of Hashem are upright, gladdening the heart.’ As we explained on what is said in Taanit 15a, ‘the righteous for light and the upright for joy’: a righteous person is one who still has work and battle to overcome the evil inclination. Such a person has no joy, for he has no rest from the evil inclination, and he needs light that Hashem will shine and reveal to him so that he can prevail. Then ‘the light of the righteous rejoices,’ for Hashem reveals to him words of Torah to straighten the heart and empty the evil from the foolish heart completely, and then he attains the level of ‘the upright for joy.’”

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 3:4: “They said to him: “But you said, ‘The abundance of the rich does not allow him to sleep.’ What does this mean? Surely it allows him to sleep, for anyone who is sated is brought to sleep by his food!” He told them: “I speak of those rich in Torah, not of those rich in money.” How so? A great person, rich in Torah, taught many students, spread Torah publicly, and was sated with Torah. Even after he dies, the students he established do not let him sleep. They sit and occupy themselves with Torah, Talmud, halakhot, and aggadot; they state laws and teachings in his name, mention his name continually, and do not let him sleep in the grave.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Toldot 38–39: “Come and see: corresponding to those seven righteous ones, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded in the Torah that an additional offering be brought on seven occasions in the year, to add delights and pleasures for them from the King’s house, so that the fathers may first be satisfied, and afterward the children. These are seven occasions, and no more. On Shabbat it corresponds to the righteous one, the foundation of the world, who is called “all” and called Shabbat, to add delights for him from the concealed mind. On the new moon it corresponds to the congregation of Israel, who is called the moon.”
